description: Given an Airflow PythonOperator/PythonVirtualenvOperator/@task running arbitrary Python (pandas, requests, boto3), author the matching Orchestra PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task — defaulting to parameters.source: INLINE with the callable body copied verbatim into parameters.code, mapping op_kwargs into inline literals or parameters.environment_variables, and correctly declining to convert a task whose entire body is actually a Slack notification.

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow task to an Orchestra pipeline task (see files/clean_inventory_snapshot.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON task running PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT with parameters.source: INLINE and parameters.code containing the drop_duplicates/available_units/filter/to_parquet body verbatim, parameters.build_command installing pandas, and connection: null since the callable needs no external credentials.

assertions.text: parameters.source is INLINE
connection is left null — no credentials are needed
build_command installs pandas for the non-stdlib import

The copied code preserves the actual transform logic (dropping duplicate skus, available_units = on_hand_units - reserved_units, keeping only non-negative available_units, writing to the curated-bucket parquet path) rather than a paraphrased summary

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow task to an Orchestra pipeline task, including how op_kwargs and the API key should come through (see files/region_sales_rollup.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON task running PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT with parameters.source: INLINE, the requests-based body copied into parameters.code, build_command installing requests, and the op_kwargs (region='us-east-1', lookback_days=7) threaded through either as inline literals in code or via parameters.environment_variables (a JSON string) rather than dropped, with SALES_API_KEY read via os.environ rather than hardcoded.

assertions.text: parameters.source is INLINE
build_command installs requests for the non-stdlib import
the region op_kwarg value is threaded through somewhere in the YAML
the lookback_days op_kwarg value is threaded through somewhere in the YAML

region ('us-east-1') and lookback_days (7) are represented as concrete inline literals in code or as parameters.environment_variables entries, not left as unresolved op_kwargs references or silently dropped
SALES_API_KEY is read via os.environ in the code (matching the source) and is not written as a literal API key value anywhere in the YAML

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow task to an Orchestra pipeline task (see files/disguised_slack_notify.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: The task's entire body posts a message via slack_sdk.WebClient(...).chat_postMessage(...) with no dedicated Slack operator — per the skill's own 'check it isn't actually a Slack task' callout, this should NOT be converted as a PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task. It should be recognized as a Slack notification and produced as (or flagged to become, per slack-airflow-to-orchestra) a SLACK task using integration_job: SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE with parameters.channel_name '#data-alerts', not a PYTHON task with the WebClient call pasted into parameters.code. SLACK_BOT_TOKEN is never written as a literal value.

assertions.text: Output is a valid YAML document
A SLACK task is present rather than the notification being left as PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT
The Slack task runs SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE
parameters.channel_name is present

The conversion correctly declines to treat this as generic Python — it does not paste the slack_sdk.WebClient(...).chat_postMessage(...) call into a PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task's parameters.code, and instead flags/converts it per slack-airflow-to-orchestra as an integration: SLACK task, recognizing that the absence of a dedicated Slack operator doesn't make this generic Python
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN is not written as a literal token value in the YAML — it's represented via a connection: reference instead

evals.prompt: Convert this task to an Orchestra pipeline task, including how the Snowflake credentials behind BaseHook.get_connection('snowflake_prod') should reach the running code (see files/snowflake_rowcount_task.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live warehouse access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON / PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task whose code reads the Snowflake credentials from the Snowflake connection *linked* on the Python connection — via orchestra.get_linked_connection("snowflake", ...) or the injected <INTEGRATION>__<CONNECTION_ID>__<FIELD> environment variables (e.g. SNOWFLAKE__PROD_12345__SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD) — rather than the Snowflake account/user/password being copied into the Python connection's own Secrets or written into the YAML. A deleted or undecryptable linked connection is skipped silently, so the code must not assume the variables are present.

assertions.text: The converted code reads the warehouse credentials from a linked connection — get_linked_connection(...) or an injected SNOWFLAKE__<CONNECTION_ID>__SNOWFLAKE_* environment variable — rather than re-declaring them
No Snowflake account/user/password value is written into the YAML
The existing Snowflake connection is linked on the Python connection instead of its credentials being copied into that connection's Secrets — the warehouse credential stays in one place

Linked-credential environment variables are named <INTEGRATION>__<CONNECTION_ID>__<FIELD>, with a double underscore between parts and the field's ID (e.g. snowflake_password) as the last part — not a single underscore or the field's display label
The code tolerates a linked connection being skipped (deleted or undecryptable credentials) rather than assuming os.environ[...] is set — e.g. .get() or an explicit presence check
